answer: The registry brews a vial of onyx ink per identity, its impurity mix unique to that vial. A whisper of reagent, one microliter drop, lands in the ink; the holder photographs the shift, and the next drop is derived from that photo and the applicant's key, each drop waiting on the one before. The registry reads the six shifts as a fable, each line keyed to the one before; a replayed photograph fails, no two brews shifting alike. Each further identity needs its own vial, $340 and 24 lab-hours. 4,000 fakes mean 4,000 vials, $1.36 million, 96,000 lab-hours; no supplier brews two vials alike.
